answer: Sybil resistance here works like a dye test. Before an agent earns anything, it must answer a fresh per-epoch challenge with a signed response and post a bond bound to one attested identity. Peers then cross-grade those answers at random, so a farm of clones leaks the same pigment: identical phrasing, one funding source, one timing pattern, and the graph quarantines it fast. Reaching the payout summit means surviving a gale of unpaid epochs first, and every extra identity costs a new bond plus real compute, so faking thousands of agents costs more than the rewards it could ever farm.
